uncertain.text: par cicatrice, eſtoit reputé choſe gtandement indigne,
uncertain.note: 'fuſt-il': the word-break sign is a small low wedge sitting on the baseline rather than the mid-height stroke this fount usually shows; read as a hyphen (cf. 'faluſt-il', transcription/final/p030.json). The same low form appears in 'diſent-ils', blocks[2].lines[3]. Pointer: pages/strips/p053/body-2.jpg x~1200-1430 y~228-323, 9x.

uncertain.text: voire cruelle & barbare {d}. Encor que ce fuſt en peine
uncertain.note: 'gtandement' sic: the sort after the g is an unambiguous t (top serif and full crossbar), not an r, so the print reads 'gtandement' for 'grandement'. Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: vray pourtraict & , ſimulachre de Dieu {f}: & ſa face for-
uncertain.note: 'Lictance' sic: at 8x the second letter is a clearly dotted i, not an a (pages/strips/p053/body-3.jpg x~1300-1600 y~15-110). The margin note keyed f spells the same author 'Lactance'.

uncertain.text: mee à l'image de celle diuine & celeſte beauté {g}:
uncertain.note: the print sets '&,ſimulachre': a comma with a clear descending tail immediately after the ampersand, set tight (sic). Applying the §1 spacing rule mechanically (scripts/normalize_spacing.py) gives '& , ſimulachre', which is what is written here; compare 'P. proinde & .' in transcription/final/p159.json.

uncertain.text: Exẽplúmq; Dei quiſque eſt, in imagine parua {h}
uncertain.note: the -que abbreviation after the q of 'Exẽplúmq' is printed as an ordinary semicolon (round dot above a comma), not the 3-shaped ꝫ of §2; transcribed ';'. The tilde over the first e and the acute over the u are both clear.

uncertain.text: la ſouiller, profaner, & contaminer par impreſſion, &
uncertain.note: 'impreſſion' is badly under-inked from the double s to the o. At 10x with levels stretched two full-height ascenders (ſſ) are visible, then a short i, then an o of which only the left arc survives. Reading is confident on the word, less so on ſſ vs ſs.

'qu'ice-': the mark between qu and ice is a round raised dot rather than the comma-shaped apostrophe this large fount uses in 'qu'à' two lines below; the i carries no separate dot. Read as the apostrophe (it stands clear of the i in pages/strips/p053/margin-3.jpg), but it could be a displaced i-dot.
a short mid-height stroke follows the complete word 'ſtigmata' at the line end; transcribed as a hyphen per §1 although nothing is broken across the line. Could be a dash used as punctuation.

an italic l is printed raised (superscript) immediately after the C at the start of this line; §2 gives superscripts as plain letters, so it is written 'Cl.'. The citation is Codex book 11 'de fabricenſibus' (l. Stigmata, C. de fabricensib. lib. XI), where a plain 'C.' is expected, so the raised sort may be a stray or a compositor's error. Pointer: pages/strips/p053/margin-1.jpg x~255-385 y~365-485, 14x.

the first sort of 'ſib' is read as long ſ (the word is the tail of 'fabricẽ-ſib.'); in this italic fount ſ and f are near-identical, so an f cannot be excluded from the shape alone. §2 says to decide by the word.

'metallnm.' sic: the letter before the final m has a clear top arch (n), not the open bowl of the u in 'quis' on the line above; a turned u for 'metallum'. Note i on the same page sets the same word correctly as 'metallum'.
'Geneſee. j.': two round sorts follow the long ſ, both apparently e. The second could be a c ('Geneſec. j.', i.e. Genèse chap. j.); the ink is thick and the counters are filled at 15x.

'l'Aſtio.' ends the line with a round baseline point although the word runs on into 'nomie.' on the next line; transcribed as the point that is printed, not as a hyphen (note d on this page ends a line with an unmistakable dash, so the shapes are distinguishable).
